cues.en: In this and the next few videos, I will introduce you to a concept and procedure called activation maximization.
cues.zh: 這部與接下來幾部影片，會介紹一個稱為活化最大化的概念與程序。

cues.en: The general idea is to use gradient descent to find a human interpretable data pattern that a single neuron in a deep learning network is tuned to.
cues.zh: 整體概念，是使用梯度下降，找出深度學習網路中某個神經元所調諧、而且人類能解讀的資料模式。

cues.en: In this video, I'll give a brief description.
cues.zh: 這部影片會先簡單描述。

cues.en: I'll show some examples from computational vision research, and then I'll discuss the assumptions underlying this method.
cues.zh: 展示計算視覺研究中的一些例子，再討論方法背後的假設。

cues.en: And then in the next few videos we will implement this technique in Python.
cues.zh: 接下來幾部，會用 Python 實作這個技巧。

cues.en: And we will consider and discuss whether llms actually conform to the assumptions of activation maximization.
cues.zh: 也會思考、討論 LLM 是否真的符合活化最大化的假設。

cues.en: So here is the motivation for this analysis method.
cues.zh: 這是這個分析方法的動機。

cues.en: Imagine this is some deep learning network.
cues.zh: 想像這是某個深度學習網路。

cues.en: Of course this is not an LLM, just a general picture of a network.
cues.zh: 當然，這不是 LLM，只是網路的一般示意圖。

cues.en: So the question is what does this one neuron here code for?
cues.zh: 問題是，這裡這個神經元編碼什麼？

cues.en: What does it pay attention to in this stimulus data.
cues.zh: 它關注刺激資料中的什麼？

cues.en: What is it tuned to?
cues.zh: 對什麼有反應偏好？

cues.en: So if you want to isolate the tuning of this one neuron, there are basically two ways that you can do that.
cues.zh: 想單獨找出這個神經元的調諧特性，基本上有兩種方式。

cues.en: One option is to show lots and lots of data samples and measure the activation that this neuron outputs.
cues.zh: 第一種，呈現大量資料樣本，測量神經元輸出的活化。

cues.en: And then you can find all of the input data samples that strongly activated this neuron.
cues.zh: 再找出所有強烈活化該神經元的輸入資料樣本。

cues.en: And then you can see if you can find some meaningful description of those data samples.
cues.zh: 接著，看看能否為這些樣本找到有意義的描述。

cues.en: A second option is to start from a random number sample, and then use gradient descent to optimize
cues.zh: 第二種，從隨機數樣本開始，再使用梯度下降，最佳化

cues.en: that random matrix so that it specifically maximizes maximizes the activation of this one neuron here.
cues.zh: 這個隨機矩陣，讓它專門最大化這個神經元的活化。

cues.en: Now both of these methods are fine.
cues.zh: 兩種方法都可以。

cues.en: They're great.
cues.zh: 都很好。

cues.en: They're used in deep learning models for Interpretability.
cues.zh: 在深度學習模型可解釋性研究中，都會使用。

cues.en: We will use this first approach a little bit later on.
cues.zh: 第一種方法，稍後會用到。

cues.en: For example, you can present lots of text to a model and see if you can find neurons that are more
cues.zh: 例如，向模型呈現大量文字，看看能否找到神經元，

cues.en: active for, let's say, past tense versus present tense, or nouns versus verbs or something like that.
cues.zh: 對過去式比現在式更活躍，或者對名詞比動詞更活躍等等。

cues.en: But this approach is more commonly used for something like mass univariate testing or linear probing with logistic regression.
cues.zh: 但這種方式，更常用於大量單變量檢定，或以邏輯斯迴歸做線性探測。

cues.en: Anyway, activation maximization refers to this second approach, and that's what we are going to do here.
cues.zh: 總之，活化最大化指的是第二種方式，這就是這裡要做的。

cues.en: It's a pretty neat approach because it's like the flipped version of how things normally work in deep learning.
cues.zh: 這個方法很有意思，因為像把深度學習平常的運作方式反過來。

cues.en: So typically you have a fixed data set and a randomly initialized model, and you use the data to train
cues.zh: 通常有固定資料集，以及隨機初始化的模型，再用資料訓練

cues.en: the model.
cues.zh: 模型。

cues.en: Now for language models, of course the data are human written text taken from the web and books and so on.
cues.zh: 對語言模型，資料當然是從網路、書籍等取得，人類寫的文字。

cues.en: And for a computer vision model, the data are pictures that you get from the web, medical images, whatever.
cues.zh: 對電腦視覺模型，資料則是網路圖片、醫學影像等等。

cues.en: The point is that typically the data are not changed and the model is optimized after being initially set to random numbers.
cues.zh: 重點是，通常資料不變，模型從隨機數初始化後，再進行最佳化。

cues.en: Now with activation maximization, we turn this whole thing around.
cues.zh: 活化最大化，則把整件事反過來。

cues.en: You start with a trained model and that is fixed.
cues.zh: 從已訓練的模型開始，並固定它。

cues.en: This is already a good working model, and you don't want to fine tune it or change the weights or anything like that.
cues.zh: 這已經是運作良好的模型，不想微調、改權重，或做其他變更。

cues.en: Instead, you start with a data sample that is randomly initialized, and then you optimize that data
cues.zh: 反而從隨機初始化的資料樣本開始，再最佳化那個資料

cues.en: matrix so that it maximally activates some feature of the model, like the activation of a particular neuron.
cues.zh: 矩陣，讓它最大程度活化模型的某個特徵，例如特定神經元的活化。

cues.en: Activation.
cues.zh: 活化

cues.en: Maximization has produced some really interesting insights in computer vision models.
cues.zh: 最大化，已為電腦視覺模型帶來一些非常有意思的洞見。

cues.en: So here you see an example of various maps that started off as random, and then we're optimized to
cues.zh: 這裡看到，各種一開始是隨機的圖，再經過最佳化，

cues.en: maximize the activation of particular neurons in different layers of a convolutional neural network.
cues.zh: 最大化卷積神經網路不同層中特定神經元的活化。

cues.en: So this is already a trained CNN that is designed to recognize image categories.
cues.zh: 這是已訓練好的 CNN，設計用來辨識影像類別。

cues.en: It's pretty neat and also a little bit spooky.
cues.zh: 相當有意思，也有點詭異。

cues.en: But you do see for example, this looks like a unit to that responds to something that looks like an eyeball.
cues.zh: 例如，這看起來像對眼球形狀有反應的單元。

cues.en: Uh, this one is like a dog unit.
cues.zh: 這個像是狗單元。

cues.en: Also down here we have some more dog neurons.
cues.zh: 下面也有更多狗神經元。

cues.en: This one here, I'm not quite sure what this is.
cues.zh: 這個，不太確定是什麼。

cues.en: This may be like a avocado cut in half.
cues.zh: 可能像切成兩半的酪梨。

cues.en: And you still see the seed in there.
cues.zh: 裡面還看得到種子。

cues.en: Anyway, I have to say, uh, that in order to get these kinds of compelling and human interpretable
cues.zh: 不過必須說，為了得到這些有說服力、能讓人解讀的

cues.en: images, you have to start with some statistical priors and do some additional tricks like dimension
cues.zh: 影像，需要先有一些統計先驗，再做額外技巧，例如維度

cues.en: compression, clustering and averaging in order to get results that look like this.
cues.zh: 壓縮、分群與平均，才能得到這樣的結果。

cues.en: In fact, if you just start from literally random noise and you try to do this activation maximization
cues.zh: 事實上，如果真的只從隨機雜訊開始，試著做活化最大化

cues.en: procedure, you tend to get results that are a little bit less human interpretable.
cues.zh: 程序，往往會得到比較不容易讓人解讀的結果。

cues.en: Now, these authors called this an example of rubbish.
cues.zh: 這些作者把它稱為垃圾範例。

cues.en: I respectfully disagree, I think this actually worked very well.
cues.zh: 我尊重他們，但不同意；我認為其實做得很好。

cues.en: It just didn't produce results that we humans can easily interpret as anything other than like curvy patches of colors.
cues.zh: 只是結果除了彎曲的彩色區塊之外，人類很難解讀成其他東西。

cues.en: But that doesn't mean that the method didn't work, and it doesn't mean that this is not the way that this particular neuron in this network sees the world.
cues.zh: 但不表示方法沒有效，也不表示這不是網路中特定神經元看待世界的方式。

cues.en: So we should not expect that the internal workings of a deep learning model are necessarily all human interpretable.
cues.zh: 所以，不應預期深度學習模型的內部運作，一定全部都能讓人解讀。

cues.en: That's not even the case for actual biological neurons inside a human brain.
cues.zh: 即使人腦內真正的生物神經元，也不是如此。

cues.en: You know, they generally do not produce activation patterns that are easily human interpretable.
cues.zh: 它們一般不會產生容易讓人解讀的活化模式。

cues.en: Of course, with some noteworthy exceptions that tend to get most of the attention in the scientific literature.
cues.zh: 當然，有些值得注意的例外，而科學文獻往往把大部分注意力放在那些例外。

cues.en: Anyway, I certainly agree that this image is not as cleanly interpretable as the ones in the previous
cues.zh: 總之，我當然同意，這張影像沒有上一張投影片中的

cues.en: slide, and in part this is because these random initializations are sometimes modified to be constrained
cues.zh: 那些那麼清楚可解讀，部分原因是，隨機初始化有時會經過修改，受到

cues.en: by strong priors, dimension compression, clustering, and other tricks that they use in this literature.
cues.zh: 強先驗、降維、分群，以及文獻中其他技巧的限制。

cues.en: So there are several assumptions that underlie this analysis.
cues.zh: 這個分析背後，有幾項假設，

cues.en: Activation maximization.
cues.zh: 也就是活化最大化。

cues.en: One assumption is that the neurons represent individual features, for example, that there is a neuron that represents an eye or a dog face or a bus.
cues.zh: 第一個假設，神經元表示個別特徵，例如有神經元表示眼睛、狗臉或公車。

cues.en: In the context of language, this assumption underlying activation maximization can be interpreted as
cues.zh: 在語言脈絡中，活化最大化背後的假設，可以解讀成

cues.en: the assumption that individual neurons code for something like a concept or a specific word, or maybe
cues.zh: 個別神經元編碼某個概念、特定單字，或者

cues.en: a group of semantically related words like banana and apple and pear.
cues.zh: 一組語意相關的單字，例如 banana、apple、pear。

cues.en: Uh, or maybe a grammatical concept like past tense.
cues.zh: 也許是過去式之類的文法概念。

cues.en: Maybe a neuron would reflect a single fact about the world.
cues.zh: 也許，一個神經元反映關於世界的某項單一事實。

cues.en: Like who was president of the US in the year 1987?
cues.zh: 例如，1987 年的美國總統是誰？

cues.en: So if this assumption is true, then activation maximization is likely to be a successful strategy.
cues.zh: 如果這個假設成立，活化最大化就可能是成功策略。

cues.en: Now, for various reasons, it turns out that this assumption is unlikely to be true, at least for lots of neurons.
cues.zh: 但出於各種原因，這個假設其實不太可能成立，至少對很多神經元如此。

cues.en: It might be the case for some individual neurons.
cues.zh: 可能對某些個別神經元成立。

cues.en: The second assumption is that activation of a unit in a deep learning network corresponds to importance.
cues.zh: 第二個假設，深度學習網路中某單元的活化，對應它的重要性。

cues.en: It is possible that the activation of a given neuron is only meaningful as it relates to the activation
cues.zh: 某個神經元的活化，可能只有在與

cues.en: of lots of other neurons, so its activation on its own might not necessarily be meaningful.
cues.zh: 其他許多神經元活化的關係中才有意義，單獨活化本身不一定有意義。

cues.en: Now, I don't want to keep comparing deep learning models to actual biological brains because they're really nothing alike.
cues.zh: 我不想一直把深度學習模型與真正生物大腦比較，因為兩者真的不像。

cues.en: They have basically nothing whatsoever in common.
cues.zh: 基本上，完全沒有共同點。

cues.en: But in biological neurons, you also see that a suppression of activity can be as informative as an increase in activity.
cues.zh: 但生物神經元中，也可以看到，活性受抑制可能和活性增加一樣有資訊。

cues.en: A third assumption is that the space that we are trying to optimize is smooth, continuous and differentiable,
cues.zh: 第三個假設，想最佳化的空間是平滑、連續、可微分的，

cues.en: and therefore optimizable at basically any step or any location in that space.
cues.zh: 因此，基本上在那個空間的任何步驟、任何位置，都能最佳化。

cues.en: Now, that actually is not necessarily the case for language.
cues.zh: 但語言其實不一定如此。

cues.en: For example, a banana and an apple are semantically closely related, but there's nothing really in between them.
cues.zh: 例如，香蕉與蘋果在語意上接近，但兩者中間並沒有什麼。

cues.en: There is no word that is one third of the way between banana and apple, and you can contrast that with
cues.zh: 沒有一個詞，位於 banana 到 apple 路程的三分之一處；相對地，

cues.en: something like color, where there really is something that is one third of the way between yellow and red.
cues.zh: 顏色則真的存在介於黃色與紅色之間三分之一處的顏色。

cues.en: The last assumption that I will mention here is that the optimized results, that is to say, the optimized
cues.zh: 最後要提的假設，是最佳化結果，也就是經過最佳化、

cues.en: random data samples that maximally activate a given neuron are human interpretable.
cues.zh: 能最大程度活化某個神經元的隨機資料樣本，是人類能解讀的。

cues.en: I've already mentioned this in the previous slide, but human interpretability is certainly something that we want.
cues.zh: 上一張投影片已提過，但人類可解釋性，確實是我們想要的。

cues.en: It's something that we look for in interpretability research, but it's not necessarily the case that
cues.zh: 這是可解釋性研究中追求的東西，但不一定

cues.en: everything inside of a model is necessarily interpretable to humans.
cues.zh: 模型內部的所有東西，都能讓人類解讀。

cues.en: Okay, so that is the brief high level intro to activation maximization.
cues.zh: 以上就是活化最大化的簡短概述。

cues.en: In the next video I will show you how to implement this technique in PyTorch using gradient descent.
cues.zh: 下一部影片，會用 PyTorch 與梯度下降，展示如何實作這個技巧。

cues.en: We will continue to think about these assumptions and whether and to what extent they hold for LMS.
cues.zh: 我們會繼續思考這些假設，以及它們是否、在多大程度上對 LLM 成立。
